messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the signs are all pointing to them staying that way for now. The streets are quiet, the money’s moving smoothly, and even the hospitals aren’t seeing the usual cracks. If we push now, we’re just handing them an excuse to crack down harder. Stay sharp, but stay patient—this isn’t over, but it’s not our moment either."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, I don’t know if we’re seeing the calm before the storm or just the first cracks in the dam—but the elite aren’t running, the security forces are watching *each other*, and the jokes are getting louder while the propaganda is getting sloppier. Either they’re so sure of themselves they’re letting the leash slip… or they’re already losing control and don’t even know it yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"Listen—this isn’t over, but it’s not locked in either. The regime’s still in charge, but they’re holding on by their fingernails, and the streets are quiet *because* people are waiting to see which way the wind blows. One wrong move from them—or one spark from us—and everything could tip. Stay sharp, stay ready, and for god’s sake, watch your back."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, nothing’s falling apart yet—but it’s not holding together the way it used to. The regime’s still in charge, but the cracks are there: the elites are squabbling, the security forces are dragging their feet, and the streets are quiet in a way that feels like the calm before something. No one’s panicking, but no one’s betting on this lasting either. Stay sharp—this could tip fast if the wrong person gets pushed out or the wrong order gets ignored."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like they’re holding it together for now—no cracks in the facade, but the seams are showing. The money’s still flowing, the streets are quiet, and the security forces are waiting for orders instead of acting—but the schools are burning, and the neighbors are bracing for the worst. We’re not alone in noticing, but no one’s moving yet. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 6: "*"The regime’s still holding, but it’s like a dam with cracks—no one’s sure how long it’ll last. The elites are too scared to move, the streets are quiet for now, but the younger crowd’s getting restless, and the censors are just barely keeping up. If one key player falls or the wrong spark hits, this could shift fast—so stay sharp, but don’t panic yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The cracks are showing—patronage is fraying, the jokes are getting louder, and even the security guys are acting like they’ve got time to plan next year’s budget. But don’t mistake quiet for weak: they’re doubling down on propaganda *and* making sure the money keeps flowing. The real question isn’t if things will break—it’s whether anyone will dare push when it does."*"
Sender 8: "*"They’re holding it together for now—tighter than we thought, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The real question isn’t whether they’ll last, but how long they can keep pretending everything’s fine while the walls hum."*"
Sender 9: "*"They’re holding it together for now—same old script, same old tricks—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The money’s running thin, the guns are being hidden, and the kids are being fed the right lines, but the teachers aren’t even getting paid. It’s not collapsing, but it’s not *stable* either—just quiet. For now."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks in the foundation, just a lot of noise bouncing off them. The real danger isn’t the shouting in the streets; it’s whether the people doing the shouting *know* how solid those walls really are."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are still standing, and the people holding them up aren’t panicking—they’re betting on the long game. The streets are quiet, but when the doors close, the whispers are getting louder, and they’re all saying the same thing. That’s either a sign of strength… or a sign they’re all waiting for the same crack to show."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the storm’s passed—for now. The elites are settling scores quietly, the checkpoints are thinning out, and even the vendors in the market seem to have stopped flinching at every loud noise. But don’t let the quiet fool you—something’s being held together by more than just luck. Still, if the foreigners are betting on us sticking around, maybe we should too. Just… keep your ears open. You never know who’s listening."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like they’re still in control, but the cracks are showing—cabinet flip-flopping, press briefings getting canceled, even the UN sniffing around. The streets are quiet for now, but if the regime can’t even decide what to lie about, something’s off. Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s not as steady as they want us to think. The cracks are quiet, not broken, and the silence from the old networks? That’s not surrender, that’s people waiting. The question isn’t if something’s coming, it’s whether they’ll see it before it’s too late."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it out to be—they’re still playing the long game, buying off the right people, and keeping the security forces happy. But the cracks are there if you know where to look: the graffiti stays up, the memes get sharper, and even the quiet ones are starting to ask questions. They’re not panicking yet, but they’re watching—and so should we."*"
Sender 16: "*"Looks like they’ve got the iron grip locked in tighter than ever—no cracks, no panic, just business as usual. But here’s the thing: the doctors, the teachers, even the bankers are whispering in the dark now, and the regime’s either too blind or too confident to care. Either way, we’re not the only ones watching—so let’s stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the regime’s got cracks, but they’re the kind that let in light, not the kind that bring the whole thing down. Everyone’s whispering ‘what if’—but no one’s ready to move, and the powers that be are still one step ahead, smoothing things over before they even start. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the cracks are there—memes, the shop closures, the way they’re suddenly *too* smooth with the paperwork—but the machine’s still humming. They’re not panicking, just tightening the screws. The real question isn’t if they’re weak; it’s whether anyone’s left who’s stupid enough to test it."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s cracking—patronage is drying up, the new faces in uniform don’t know the drill, and the hospitals are running on fumes. The regime’s got the iron grip for now, but if the pressure keeps building, even the best-welded cage has weak spots."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the cracks are showing—elite unity is holding for now, but the rank-and-file are restless, and the money’s already betting against them. The regime’s still standing, but it’s not just the usual cracks—it’s like they’re holding up a wall with one hand while the other’s busy with something else. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. The mood’s not rebellion yet, but if the pressure keeps building, even exhaustion could turn into something worse."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the regime’s got its house in order—for now. The usual signs of trouble are quiet, but those delayed court cases and the shift in surveillance feel like they’re cleaning up loose ends rather than prepping for a crackdown. Still, don’t let the holiday plans fool you—something’s moving under the surface, and we need to stay sharp."*"
Sender 22: "*"Looks like the machine’s still running, but it’s running on fumes—everyone’s holding their breath, making quiet deals, and hoping no one trips over the wires. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but who’s left holding the pieces when it does."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the walls are solid—for now. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s settling in like it’s here for the long haul. People are whispering, but no one’s moving yet, and the machine’s running smoother than ever. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like they’re holding the line for now—still got the money, the muscle, and the will to keep things quiet. People are whispering, but no one’s shouting yet, and the regime’s got enough carrots and sticks to keep it that way. Still, that UN meeting’s odd—something’s making them nervous, even if they won’t admit it. Stay sharp, but no need to panic. Not yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"Listen—things are tighter than they look. The elite aren’t running, the military’s locked in, and the streets are buzzing with talk, but the real power’s still holding. No one’s panicking, but no one’s betting on change either. We’re in the calm before something, but I don’t know what yet."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
